theory.title: Quantifying expressions: a great deal of, a large number of, hardly any, plenty of
theory.explanation: Use a large number of with plural countable nouns, a great deal of with uncountable nouns, plenty of with both, and hardly any to express a very small amount or number.
theory.tip: Countable plural: a large number of. Uncountable: a great deal of. Plenty of funciona con ambos.

content.passage: The community survey showed that a large number of residents wanted better recycling facilities. A great deal of support was offered by local businesses, and plenty of volunteers agreed to help. However, there was hardly any space near the market for new containers. The council is now looking for a suitable location. The project still needs a large amount of funding, but organisers believe there is plenty of interest in the idea.

I hope that by the next few years we will have made further progress.
